title: Arancini
summary: Cold risotto balls around mozzarella and ragù, crumbed and fried until golden.

ingredientGroups.title: Risotto base (or use 3 cups leftover risotto)

items.raw: 900ml chicken stock (or vegetable stock), kept warm

steps.text: Cook the risotto: sweat the onion in butter for 5 minutes. Add the rice and toast 2 minutes. Add wine; reduce. Add stock a ladle at a time, stirring, until rice is al dente, 16 minutes. Stir in the parmesan. Spread on a tray to cool quickly, then refrigerate until cold, ideally overnight.

Take a heaped tablespoon of cold risotto. Flatten in your palm. Place a cube of mozzarella, a bit of ragu, and a few peas in the centre. Top with more risotto and shape into a tight ball about the size of a golf ball.
Roll each ball in flour, then egg, then panko, press the panko on firmly.
Heat oil to 175°C. Fry the arancini in batches for 4 minutes, rolling, until deep golden all over. Drain on a rack.
Serve hot with warm marinara for dipping and lemon wedges.

notes: Cold risotto holds its shape; warm risotto falls apart. Make the risotto the night before.
A wet hand keeps the risotto from sticking when shaping. Keep a small bowl of water nearby.

title: Arepas
summary: Crisp cornmeal rounds split and stuffed with a creamy avocado and chicken filling.

items.raw: 300g pre-cooked white cornmeal (P.A.N. or Harina P.A.N. brand)

steps.text: In a bowl, mix the cornmeal, water, salt, and oil with your hand. Knead for 2 minutes, the dough should be soft and smooth, not sticky. Rest 5 minutes.
Mix the reina pepiada: combine chicken, avocado, mayo, lime, coriander, spring onion, salt, and pepper.
Divide the dough into 8 balls. Flatten each between damp hands to a 1.5cm disc, 8cm wide. Smooth any cracks at the edges.
Heat a dry non-stick pan or griddle over medium heat. Cook the arepas 5 minutes a side until a deep golden crust forms. They should sound hollow when tapped.
Move to a 180°C oven for 8 more minutes to cook through (or keep on the heat longer).
Split each arepa horizontally like a pita pocket. Stuff with reina pepiada, a small pile of cheese, and tomato. Top with hot sauce.

notes: Pre-cooked cornmeal (masarepa) is non-negotiable. Regular cornmeal won't work.
Crisp on the outside, soft inside, that contrast is the whole point.

title: Avocado Toast
summary: Garlic-rubbed sourdough under a thick layer of smashed avocado, lemon and chilli.

items.raw: 4 thick slices good sourdough (or seeded bread)

steps.text: Toast the bread until deeply golden and crisp, substantial toast, not pale.
While warm, rub the cut side of the garlic clove over each slice. The toast grates the garlic.
Halve the avocados. Scoop the flesh into a bowl. Add lemon juice, a generous pinch of salt, and pepper. Smash with a fork, leave it chunky, not pureed.
Pile the avocado onto each toast. Don't spread thin, go thick.
Drizzle with olive oil. Scatter chilli flakes, lemon zest, and more flaky salt.
Top with your chosen extras. Eat immediately, toast goes soft fast.

notes: Garlic rub on warm toast is the single most underrated move. It adds a layer without overwhelming.
Avocado should hold its shape, not be pureed. Texture matters.

Soft-boiled eggs and smoked salmon: if you're pregnant, cooking for young children or older people, or have a weakened immune system, boil the eggs until the yolks are firm and skip the smoked salmon.

title: Baked Cod
summary: Cod baked under a herby parmesan crumb, with a lemon, caper and white wine butter.

steps.text: Heat oven to 200°C. Pat cod dry, season, brush with olive oil. Place on a lined tray.
Mix panko, parmesan, herbs, garlic, lemon zest, melted butter, salt, pepper.
Press a thick layer of crumb onto each cod fillet.
Bake 14 minutes until the cod flakes and the crumb is deep golden.
For sauce: melt butter, sizzle garlic 30 seconds. Add wine, reduce 90 seconds. Add lemon juice, capers, parsley.
Plate each cod fillet, spoon sauce around (not over the crumb).

notes: Sauce around, not over. Keep the crumb crisp.
Cod is delicate. Don't flip in the pan, bake it straight.

title: Baked Salmon
summary: Salmon baked under a lemon, dill and garlic butter that becomes its own sauce.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Pat the salmon dry. Drizzle with olive oil and season.
Mix the butter ingredients into a soft paste.
Lay the salmon skin-side-down on a foil-lined tray. Spread a generous spoon of lemon-dill butter on top of each fillet.
Bake 14–16 minutes, the salmon should be just opaque in the centre and a knife should slide through with no resistance. The butter melts into a sauce around it.
Spoon the buttery pan juices back over each fillet before plating.
Serve with asparagus, potatoes, and lemon.

notes: Slightly under is better than over. Salmon goes from perfect to dry in 2 minutes.
Butter melts into a self-saucing dish. No extra sauce needed.

title: Baked Ziti
summary: Pasta baked with sausage ragù, pockets of ricotta and a golden mozzarella top.

items.raw: 400g Italian sausage, casings removed (or beef mince)

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cook the pasta in well-salted water 3 minutes less than packet (it bakes more). Drain.
In a wide pan, brown the sausage in oil for 5 minutes. Add onion; cook 5 minutes. Add garlic and chilli; cook 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the passata, tomatoes, oregano, and sugar. Simmer 10 minutes. Season.
In a bowl, mix the ricotta with the egg, parmesan, basil, and a pinch of salt.
Toss the drained pasta with two-thirds of the sauce.
Spread a thin layer of sauce in a baking dish. Tip in half the pasta. Dollop half the ricotta mix in spoonfuls. Scatter half the mozzarella.
Repeat: pasta, ricotta dollops, mozzarella. Spoon the remaining sauce around the edges.
Bake 25 minutes until the top is golden and bubbling. Optional: 2 minutes under the grill for extra char.
Rest 10 minutes before serving.

notes: Undercook the pasta. It finishes in the oven and will go to mush if started al dente.
Ricotta dolloped in pockets, not stirred through. You want creamy surprises.

title: Baked Zucchini Boats
summary: Zucchini halves filled with spiced mince and tomato, baked under melted mozzarella.

steps.text: Heat oven to 200°C. Scoop out the centre flesh from each zucchini half with a teaspoon, leaving a 1cm shell. Chop the scooped flesh.
Brush boats with oil. Season. Roast cut-side-up 12 minutes to pre-soften.
For filling: brown mince in oil 5 minutes. Add onion; 5 minutes. Add garlic, tomato paste, spices; 1 minute. Add the chopped zucchini flesh and passata. Simmer 10 minutes. Season.
Spoon filling into the boats. Top with mozzarella and parmesan.
Bake 15 minutes until cheese is melted and golden.
Scatter parsley.

notes: Pre-roast the boats. Filling on raw zucchini stays watery and bitter.
Use the scooped flesh in the filling, no waste.

title: Bangers and Mash
summary: Butcher's sausages in a slow caramelised onion gravy over mustardy mash.

steps.text: Boil potatoes in salted water until very tender, 18 minutes.
Melt butter and oil in a wide heavy pan. Add the onions and sugar. Cook 25 minutes over medium-low heat, stirring, until deep caramel.
Push onions to one side. Add the sausages. Brown all over for 8 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over the onions. Stir 1 minute.
Pour in the stock gradually. Add Worcestershire, mustard, and thyme. Simmer 10 minutes until the gravy thickens and the sausages are cooked through (75°C in the centre).
Drain potatoes well. Mash with butter, milk, sour cream, and mustard. Season.
Pile mash on plates. Sit 2 sausages on top. Ladle plenty of onion gravy over. Spoon peas alongside.

notes: Good sausages matter, supermarket bangers wreck the dish. Find a butcher.
Deep caramelised onions = deep gravy. There's no shortcut.

title: Banh Mi
summary: Caramelised lemongrass pork in a crisp roll with pickled carrot, daikon and coriander.

items.raw: 500g pork shoulder, sliced thin (or pork belly)
4 small Vietnamese baguettes (or short crusty rolls)

steps.text: Whisk the pickle brine ingredients. Tip the carrot and daikon in. Press down and rest 30 minutes (or up to 3 days in the fridge).
Whisk the pork marinade. Toss with the sliced pork. Rest 20 minutes.
Heat a heavy pan over high heat. Cook the pork in single-layer batches for 2 minutes a side until caramelised at the edges. Keep warm.
Split the baguettes lengthways without cutting all the way through. Briefly warm them in a 200°C oven for 3 minutes, soft inside, crisp outside.
Spread mayo on the inside of each baguette. Add a thin smear of pâté if using.
Layer: cucumber, pork (with juices), pickled carrot-daikon, coriander, chilli. Dash a few drops of Maggi seasoning down the line.
Press the baguette together gently. Eat immediately while crisp.

notes: Crisp outside, pillowy inside, that's a banh mi roll. Soft hot-dog buns ruin it.
Maggi seasoning is a Vietnamese staple. Don't skip, it adds the umami pop.

title: BBQ Chicken Pizza
summary: Barbecue-sauced chicken, bacon and red onion on a crisp base, finished with coriander.

items.raw: 2 pizza bases (or homemade pizza dough for 2)
4 rashers streaky bacon, fried crisp and broken

steps.text: Heat the oven to 230°C with a pizza stone or heavy tray inside.
Toss the shredded chicken with 4 tbsp BBQ sauce until coated.
Stretch each base. Spread the rest of the BBQ sauce thinly to within 2cm of the edge.
Dot with mozzarella. Scatter BBQ chicken, red onion slices.
Slide onto the hot stone. Bake 8–10 minutes until the crust is deep golden and the cheese is bubbling.
Scatter crisp bacon and coriander. Drizzle a little more BBQ sauce.
Slice and serve.

notes: Less is more with BBQ sauce. Too much makes a sloppy pizza.
Coriander on top divides people. Use parsley if you're a coriander hater.

title: BBQ Pulled Chicken
summary: Seared chicken thighs braised in a homemade barbecue sauce and shredded for soft rolls.

items.item: Soft burger buns or slider rolls
items.raw: Soft burger buns or slider rolls

steps.text: Rub the chicken with oil, salt, paprika, garlic powder, pepper. Sear in a hot pan 3 minutes a side until golden.
Combine all BBQ sauce ingredients in a heavy pot. Simmer 5 minutes.
Add the seared chicken to the sauce. Cover and braise on low heat for 45–60 minutes, turning occasionally, until the chicken is falling apart.
Lift the chicken out. Shred with 2 forks.
Return shreds to the sauce. Toss to coat, the chicken should be glossy, not swimming.
Pile onto soft buns with slaw on top and pickles on the side.

notes: Sear first, then braise. Char before stew.
BBQ sauce from scratch is 5 minutes of work and tastes 10x better than the bottle.

title: BBQ Ribs
summary: Pork spare ribs rubbed, roasted low, braised in foil and glazed in barbecue sauce.

items.raw: 2 racks American-style pork spare ribs (about 1.5kg total)

steps.text: On the underside of each rack, slip a butter knife under the membrane at one end. Grab it with a paper towel and pull off in one sheet. Skipping this = chewy ribs.
Combine the rub ingredients. Coat each rack heavily on all sides, pressing it in. Rest 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 135°C. Place ribs bone-side-down on a rack over a foil-lined tray. Roast for 2.5 hours, undisturbed.
Tear off two large sheets of heavy foil. On each, place 2 tbsp butter, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 2 tbsp honey, and a splash of apple juice. Lay a rack on top, bone-side-up, and seal tightly into a packet.
Return to the oven for 1 hour. The wrap braises the meat tender, this is the "Texas crutch".
Combine the BBQ sauce ingredients in a small pan. Simmer 8 minutes.
Unwrap the ribs (careful, hot liquid). Brush both sides with sauce. Return to a clean rack, bone-side-down, and bake uncovered at 175°C for 20 minutes to set the glaze. Brush again halfway.
Rest 10 minutes. Cut between the bones into individual ribs.

notes: The 3-2-1 method (smoke 3hr, wrap 2hr, sauce 1hr) is the gold standard for smoking. This oven version compresses it but follows the same logic.
A rib should bend in half before snapping, not fall off the bone. Falling off is overcooked.

title: BBQ Ribs Plate
summary: Rubbed, foil-braised and glazed pork ribs served with slaw, cornbread and pickles.

steps.text: Remove the silver membrane from the underside of each rack.
Mix rub. Coat ribs heavily, press in. Rest 30 minutes.
Heat oven to 135°C. Place ribs bone-side-down on a rack over a foil-lined tray. Roast 2.5 hours.
Tear foil sheets. On each, place 2 tbsp butter, 2 tbsp brown sugar, 2 tbsp honey, apple juice. Lay a rack bone-side-up. Seal tight.
Return to oven for 1 hour.
Simmer BBQ sauce ingredients 8 minutes.
Unwrap. Brush ribs with sauce. Return to rack, bone-side-down, bake uncovered at 175°C for 20 minutes to set the glaze. Brush again halfway.
Rest 10 minutes. Cut between bones into individual ribs.
Plate up: a pile of ribs, coleslaw, cornbread, pickles, mac and cheese, jalapeños on the side.

notes: Same ribs as the standalone BBQ Ribs, this version is the "plate" with classic American sides.
A rib should bend before snapping, not fall apart. Falling apart is overcooked.

title: Beef Bourguignon
summary: Chuck braised in burgundy, the sauce strained and reduced, with onions and mushrooms.

items.raw: 1 bottle (750ml) good pinot noir (or red burgundy)

steps.text: Pat the beef dry, season heavily, and brown in oil over high heat in batches. Don't crowd or it steams.
In the same pot, render the bacon for 4 minutes. Add the carrots and onions; cook 8 minutes. Add the garlic for the last minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and flour. Cook 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine and stock. Scrape the base. Add the bay and thyme.
Return the beef. Bring to a bare simmer. Cover and braise in a 150°C oven for 2.5 hours, stirring once midway. The beef should yield to a fork.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a pan over medium heat. Add the pearl onions and brown for 8 minutes. Add the mushrooms; cook 5 minutes. Salt lightly.
When the beef is done, lift the chunks onto a plate. Strain the sauce, pressing the solids. Return the sauce to the pot and reduce on high heat for 10 minutes until glossy.
Return the beef, fold in the onions and mushrooms. Simmer 5 minutes to marry.
Scatter parsley. Serve with mashed potato or crusty bread.

notes: Strain the sauce midway through, then reduce. That's the move that turns rustic stew into proper bourguignon.
Best made a day ahead, the flavour deepens.

title: Beef Brisket
summary: Whole brisket rubbed with salt and pepper, cooked low for hours, wrapped and rested.

items.item: apple cider vinegar in a spray bottle
items.raw: 250ml apple cider vinegar in a spray bottle
BBQ sauce (optional, proper brisket needs no sauce)
items.note: optional, proper brisket needs no sauce

steps.text: Trim the brisket: leave a 5mm fat cap, remove any hard chunks of fat from the underside.
Combine the rub ingredients (except the spray bottle). Coat the brisket heavily on all sides. Rest at room temperature 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 130°C. Place the brisket fat-side-up on a rack over a deep tray.
Cook for 6 hours, spraying with apple cider vinegar every hour after the first 2. The bark should be deep mahogany.

After 6 hours, check the internal temperature. When it stalls around 70°C, wrap tightly in butcher paper or foil. Return to the oven for 1–2 more hours until it reads 95°C and a probe slides in like butter.
Rest the brisket wrapped, in a cool oven (off, with the door cracked), for 1 hour minimum, this is non-negotiable. Resting redistributes the juices.
Slice across the grain (the flat) at 5mm thick. The point can be cubed for burnt ends.
Serve with rolls, slaw, pickles. Or piled on Texas toast.

notes: Probe tender, not "an hour per kilo". The stall and the rest are the whole technique.
Slice across the grain or it eats tough. Look at the muscle fibres before cutting.

title: Beef Bulgogi Bowl
summary: Pear-marinated bulgogi over rice with seasoned vegetables, kimchi and a fried egg.

items.raw: 700g beef rib eye (or sirloin), sliced paper-thin
1 cup spinach, blanched and seasoned with sesame oil and salt
items.prep: blanched and seasoned with sesame oil and salt

items.raw: Gochujang sauce (3 tbsp gochujang, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp rice vinegar)
items.note: 3 tbsp gochujang, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp rice vinegar

steps.text: Mix the marinade. Toss with the beef. Rest 30 minutes.
While the beef marinates, cook the rice, blanch the spinach and bean sprouts, and quickly sauté the carrot. Fry the eggs just before serving.
Heat a wide pan over screaming-high heat. Cook the beef in batches in a single layer for 90 seconds per batch, quick sear, the marinade glazes.
Mix the gochujang sauce.
Build each bowl: rice on the bottom. Arrange bulgogi in the centre, then spinach, bean sprouts, carrot, kimchi, fried egg in coloured sections.
Drizzle gochujang sauce over. Scatter sesame and spring onion.
Eat by mixing it all together at the table.

notes: Korean bibimbap-style bowl with bulgogi as the protein. Different sections of veg = a complete plate.
Grated pear is the secret tenderiser.

title: Beef Burrito
summary: Spiced beef, lime rice, beans and cheese rolled tight and toasted in the pan.

items.raw: 1 tin black beans, drained and warmed

steps.text: Brown the mince in oil over high heat for 6 minutes. Add onion; cook 5 minutes. Add garlic and spices; cook 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and stock. Simmer 5 minutes until glossy and almost dry. Lime juice and seasoning at the end.
Mix the rice with coriander, lime, oil, and salt.
On each warm tortilla, layer down the centre: rice, beef, beans, cheese, avocado, pico, sour cream, jalapeños. Don't overfill, a tight burrito beats a busy one.
Fold the bottom up, fold the sides in tight, then roll forward firmly. Place seam-side-down.
Toast each burrito seam-side-down in a dry pan for 90 seconds per side to seal and crisp.
Cut in half on the diagonal. Serve with extra salsa.

notes: Wet ingredients in the middle, dry on the outside. Wet against the tortilla makes it tear.
Toast the wrap to seal, burritos that don't hold together are a tragedy.

title: Beef Curry
summary: Chuck braised slowly with deep-browned onion, whole spices and tomato until spoon-tender.

steps.text: Brown the beef in 2 tbsp ghee over high heat in batches. Set aside.
In the same pot, add remaining ghee. Cook onions 12 minutes until deep golden, the foundation flavour.
Add garlic, ginger, and whole spices (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, bay). Cook 1 minute.
Add ground spices and tomato paste. Toast 1 minute.
Add the blitzed tomatoes. Cook 8 minutes until the oil splits.
Return beef. Pour in stock. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and braise on lowest heat (or 150°C oven) for 2 hours, stirring every 30 minutes.
Stir in garam masala. Season. Rest 10 minutes for flavours to settle.
Top with coriander. Serve over rice (or with naan) and yogurt.

notes: Deep brown onions = deep curry. Don't rush it.
A long slow braise turns chuck into spoon-tender bites.

title: Beef Enchiladas
summary: Spiced beef rolled in sauce-dipped corn tortillas and baked in dried chilli sauce.

items.raw: 4 dried guajillo chillies, stems and seeds removed
2 dried ancho chillies, stems and seeds removed

steps.text: Toast the dried chillies in a dry pan over medium heat for 30 seconds a side. Soak in just-boiled water for 15 minutes.
Drain the chillies. Blend with the oil, onion, garlic, cumin, oregano, and 250ml stock until smooth.
Tip the puree into a pan with the rest of the stock. Simmer 8 minutes until darkened. Season.
Brown the beef in oil for 6 minutes. Add the onion; cook 4 minutes. Add garlic and all the spices; cook 1 minute. Add tomato paste; cook 1 minute. Season heavily.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Spread a ladle of red sauce in the base of a baking dish.
Warm each tortilla briefly. Dip each in the warm sauce, then place on a board. Spoon beef along the centre and a small sprinkle of cheese. Roll up.
Lay seam-down in the dish, tight together.
Pour the rest of the sauce over the top. Scatter with the remaining cheese.
Bake 20 minutes until bubbling and the cheese is golden in spots.
Top with feta, red onion, coriander, sour cream, and jalapeños.

notes: Dried chillies make the sauce. Tinned enchilada sauce is fine but not the same dish.
Dip the tortillas in sauce before rolling, this is what stops them tearing in the oven.

title: Beef Korma
summary: Chuck braised gently with yoghurt, browned onion and cashews in a mild, fragrant sauce.

items.raw: 80g cashews, soaked 15 minutes then blended smooth with 200ml water
items.prep: soaked 15 minutes then blended smooth with 200ml water

items.raw: Pinch of saffron in 2 tbsp warm milk (optional)

steps.text: Mix the beef with yogurt, ginger garlic paste, turmeric, and salt. Rest 1 hour.
In a heavy pot, melt 3 tbsp ghee. Cook the onions slowly for 25 minutes over medium-low until deep mahogany. This colour and sweetness is the dish.
Lift out half the onions and reserve for finishing. Blend the rest with a splash of water to a smooth paste.
Return paste to the pot with the remaining ghee. Add the whole spices and bay. Cook 1 minute.
Add the ground spices. Toast 30 seconds.
Add the marinated beef. Stir to coat. Cook 5 minutes.
Pour in 250ml water. Cover and braise on the lowest heat for 90 minutes, stirring every 20 minutes.
Add the cashew paste. Simmer 15 minutes.
Off the heat, stir in the cream and saffron milk. Sprinkle garam masala. Rest 5 minutes.
Top with reserved onions and coriander. Serve with rice and naan.

notes: No tomatoes in a real korma, it's yogurt and cashew based, milder and more aromatic than other curries.
Deep brown onions and the cashew paste are what makes the sauce silky and rich.

title: Beef Lasagna
summary: A beef and red wine ragù layered with béchamel and cheese, rested so it slices cleanly.

steps.text: Brown the beef in olive oil for 6 minutes. Add onion, carrot, celery; cook 10 minutes. Add garlic; cook 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes. Add the wine and reduce by half. Add passata, tomatoes, milk, bay, oregano. Simmer on lowest heat 60 minutes until thick and glossy.
Make bechamel: melt butter, whisk in flour, cook 2 minutes. Whisk in warm milk gradually. Cook 8 minutes until thick. Season with nutmeg, salt, white pepper.
Heat the oven to 190°C.
Build in a deep dish: thin ragu, sheets, ragu, bechamel, mozzarella + parmesan. Repeat to make 4 layers in all. Finish bechamel + heavy parmesan.
Bake 40 minutes until deeply golden and bubbling.
Rest 20 minutes before cutting, this is non-negotiable.

notes: Beef-only ragu (vs spaghetti bolognese which is beef-pork), slightly leaner, slightly cleaner.
The 20-minute rest sets the layers. Cut earlier and it slides.

title: Beef Noodle Soup
summary: Beef shin braised in a spiced chilli bean broth, served over wheat noodles with greens.

items.raw: 1 small bunch bok choy (or gai lan)

steps.text: Blanch beef: cover with cold water, bring to a boil, simmer 5 minutes, drain, rinse.
In a heavy pot, heat oil. Cook garlic, ginger, and spring onion whites 2 minutes.
Add tomatoes. Cook 4 minutes until breaking down.
Add doubanjiang. Fry 2 minutes until the oil turns red.
Add beef. Stir to coat. Add Shaoxing wine, both soys, sugar, star anise, cinnamon, dried chillies, Sichuan peppercorns.
Pour in stock. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook on lowest heat for 2 hours, until the beef is fork-tender.
In the last 10 minutes, cook the noodles in boiling water per packet. Blanch the greens 90 seconds.
Divide noodles into deep bowls. Top with greens and a generous ladle of broth and beef.
Top with spring onion greens, pickled greens, and a spoon of chilli oil.

notes: Doubanjiang is what makes Taiwanese beef noodle soup distinct from Pho or Korean. Don't substitute.
Blanching the beef first gives a clean broth. Skip it and you get foam-scum.

title: Beef Pho
summary: A quick spiced and charred-onion beef broth poured over noodles and raw fillet.

items.raw: 2 brown onions, halved and charred (under grill or over flame)
300g eye fillet, sliced paper-thin (freeze first 30 min)

steps.text: Char the onion and ginger directly over a gas flame (or under a hot grill) until blackened in patches.
Toast the star anise, cinnamon, cloves, coriander seeds, and cardamom in a dry pan for 2 minutes.
In a pot, combine the stock, charred aromatics, toasted spices, fish sauce, sugar, and salt. Simmer 45 minutes, never a hard boil.
Strain the broth through fine mesh.
Soak the rice noodles in hot water for 8 minutes until pliable. Drain into bowls.
Lay the raw eye fillet over the noodles. Top with sliced onion.
Bring the broth back to a rolling boil. Ladle straight over the beef and noodles, it cooks the meat in seconds.
Bring herbs, sprouts, chilli, lime, and sauces to the table on a platter. Each diner builds their own.

notes: This is the quick weeknight pho, full-bone-broth pho takes 3 hours but starts with high-quality stock.
Freezing the eye fillet for 30 minutes makes paper-thin slicing easy with any sharp knife.

title: Beef Rendang
summary: Chuck cooked for hours in spiced coconut until the liquid is gone and the beef is dark.

items.raw: 6 dried red chillies, soaked in hot water
60g toasted desiccated coconut (kerisik), ground to a paste

steps.text: Blitz all spice paste ingredients to a smooth paste. Patience, it takes a few minutes.
Heat the oil in a wide heavy pot over medium heat. Fry the spice paste for 8–10 minutes, stirring constantly, until the oil splits and the paste smells nutty and toasted.
Add the beef. Stir to coat. Cook 5 minutes.
Pour in the coconut milk, coconut cream, water, lime leaves, lemongrass, cinnamon, cloves, and star anise. Stir well.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook uncovered, stirring every 15 minutes, for 2 hours. The liquid will reduce by half and turn caramel-brown.
Add the palm sugar, tamarind, salt, and toasted ground coconut (kerisik). Stir well.

Continue cooking uncovered, stirring more frequently now, for another 60–90 minutes. The rendang is done when the liquid has completely reduced, the oil has separated, and the beef is dark brown and coated in a thick spice paste. Stir constantly in the last 20 minutes, it sticks fast.
Taste and adjust salt or palm sugar. Rest 15 minutes, flavour deepens.
Serve over rice with chilli and fried shallots.

notes: Real rendang is dry, not saucy. You're evaporating all liquid until only spiced oil and meat remain.
Kerisik (toasted ground coconut) is the secret, adds a deep nutty richness. Toast desiccated coconut in a dry pan until brown, then grind.

title: Beef Roast Dinner
summary: Garlic-studded beef roasted over vegetables, the tray juices reduced to gravy.

steps.text: Bring beef to room temp. Cut slits all over. Push slivers of garlic into them.
Rub with oil, herbs, salt, pepper.
Heat the oven to 220°C.

Boil the potatoes in salted water for 10 minutes. Drain, then shake in the colander to rough up the edges. Heat the duck fat in a second roasting tray in the oven for 5 minutes, add the potatoes, turn to coat, and roast alongside the beef.
Sear the beef in a hot pan all over for 5 minutes.
Place beef in a roasting tray with the vegetables around. Pour stock and wine around (not over) the beef.
Roast 20 minutes at 220°C, then drop to 180°C for 40 minutes (medium-rare, 52°C internal).
Rest the beef 20 minutes on a board, tented with foil. Meanwhile, turn the oven back up to 220°C and roast the potatoes until crisp and golden.
Strain the pan juices. Reduce to a syrup if needed. That's your gravy.
Slice the beef across the grain. Plate with roasted veg, potatoes, gravy, and mustard.

notes: Resting redistributes the juices. Cut early and they run out onto the board, not into your mouth.
Across the grain. Always look at the muscle fibres before cutting.

title: Beef Shawarma Plate
summary: Thin spiced beef seared fast and piled on rice with hummus, tabbouleh and tahini.

items.raw: 800g beef sirloin (or rump), sliced thin against the grain
Saffron basmati rice (or plain basmati rice)

steps.text: Marinate beef with all listed ingredients at least 2 hours.
Heat a heavy pan over screaming-high heat. Cook beef in batches in a single layer for 90 seconds per batch, quick char on the edges, still tender inside.
Plate: rice on one side, beef on top in a tight pile. Surround with hummus, tabbouleh, pickles.
Drizzle with tahini sauce and toum. Dust beef with sumac. Scatter parsley. Squeeze lemon. Pita on the side.

notes: Sliced thin against the grain, hot fast cook. Like a Middle-Eastern stir-fry.
Sumac on the beef is the finishing touch, gives a lemony tang without lemon juice.

title: Beef Stroganoff
summary: Seared beef strips in a mushroom, mustard and sour cream sauce, served over noodles.

items.raw: 600g beef fillet (or rump steak), sliced into 1cm strips against the grain
items.prep: sliced into 1cm strips against the grain

items.raw: Buttered pappardelle (or egg noodles or rice)

steps.text: Pat the beef bone-dry, season with salt and pepper. Sear in oil over screaming-high heat in batches, 60 seconds total per batch. The beef should be brown outside, pink inside. Lift out.
Reduce heat to medium. Melt the butter in the same pan. Cook the onion 5 minutes until softened.
Add the mushrooms and cook 8 minutes until deep brown and any liquid has evaporated, patience here makes the dish.
Add the garlic and paprika; cook 1 minute. Sprinkle the flour and stir for 2 minutes.
Pour in the wine. Scrape the base. Add the stock, mustard, and Worcestershire. Simmer 5 minutes until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Off the heat, whisk in the sour cream, adding it off the heat stops it splitting.
Return the beef and any resting juices. Warm through gently (don't boil). 1 minute.
Plate over noodles or rice. Scatter parsley and dill.

notes: Sear hot and fast, finish off-heat. Boiled-in-sauce beef goes grey.
Sour cream off the heat or it curdles. Hard rule.

title: Beef Tacos
summary: Well-browned spiced mince in charred corn tortillas with lime, avocado and feta.

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan over high heat. Add the mince and break it up. Brown for 6–8 minutes, really let it crust on the base before stirring, that's where the flavour comes from.
Push the meat to one side. Add the onion to the empty space and cook 3 minutes until soft. Add the garlic for the last minute.
Stir everything together with the tomato paste, cumin, paprika, oregano, chilli, and coriander. Toast for 1 minute, the spices should bloom and smell nutty.
Pour in the stock. Simmer for 5–8 minutes until the liquid has nearly evaporated and the beef is glossy. Finish with lime juice. Taste for salt.
Char the tortillas directly over a gas flame or in a dry pan for 20 seconds a side. Stack them in a clean tea towel to keep soft.
Build at the table: tortilla, beef, avocado, red onion, coriander, jalapeños, a squeeze of lime, a smear of sour cream, a scatter of feta.

notes: Double-stack tortillas if they're thin, corn tears easily under wet fillings.

title: Beef Tikka
summary: Yoghurt-marinated beef skewers roasted hot and charred, kept pink in the middle.

steps.text: Combine all marinade ingredients with the beef. Rest 4 hours minimum, ideally overnight.
Soak bamboo skewers or use metal. Thread the beef cubes leaving small gaps for char.
Heat the oven to 240°C with rack on top. Line a tray with foil and set a rack inside.
Place skewers on the rack. Roast 10 minutes for medium, turning once. Edges should char.
Finish under a hot grill (broiler) for 2 minutes per side for proper char.
Rest 3 minutes. Serve with naan, chutney, sliced onion.

notes: Sirloin or rump, don't overcook past medium. Beef tikka should still be pink inside.
Yogurt and acid in the marinade tenderise overnight.
Start the day before: the beef marinates overnight.

title: Beef Wellington
summary: Seared fillet wrapped in duxelles, prosciutto and puff pastry, baked to mahogany.

steps.text: Tie the beef with kitchen twine at 4cm intervals so it holds shape. Season heavily.
Heat oil in a heavy pan over high heat. Sear the fillet on every side, including the ends, for 2 minutes each, a deep crust is what you're after, not cooking it through.
Rest the beef on a tray, untie the twine, brush all over with mustard, and refrigerate while you make the duxelles.

Cook the mushrooms, shallots, and garlic in butter over medium-high heat with a pinch of salt. Stir constantly for 10 minutes until all liquid evaporates and you have a thick, dry paste. Add the sherry and thyme. Cook another 2 minutes. Cool completely.
Lay cling film on the bench. Arrange the prosciutto in overlapping slices into a sheet large enough to wrap the beef.
Spread the cold duxelles over the prosciutto in an even layer. Place the beef along one edge.
Using the cling film, roll the prosciutto and duxelles tightly around the beef. Twist the ends of the cling film like a sausage to compress. Refrigerate 30 minutes.
Roll the puff pastry to a rectangle large enough to wrap the parcel.
Unwrap the cling film. Place the beef on the pastry. Brush exposed pastry with egg yolk and fold it over, pressing to seal. Trim excess. Turn seam-side down.
Brush the entire pastry with egg yolk. Score gently with a knife in a crosshatch (just the surface, don't cut through). Sprinkle with flaky salt.
Bake at 220°C for 35–40 minutes. A meat thermometer in the centre should read 50°C for rare, 55°C for medium-rare. The pastry should be deep mahogany.
Rest 10 minutes. Slice with a serrated knife, 2cm slices show off the layers.

notes: Dry duxelles or soggy pastry. The mushroom mixture must be a thick paste with no moisture left.
Refrigeration between every step keeps the pastry crisp and stops it tearing.

title: Bibimbap
summary: Rice crowned with separately cooked vegetables, seared beef, a fried egg and gochujang.

items.item: Sesame oil and salt for seasoning each
items.raw: Sesame oil and salt for seasoning each
2 garlic cloves, divided across the veg

steps.text: Combine the beef with its marinade and rest 15 minutes.
Whisk the gochujang sauce ingredients together. Done.

Cook each vegetable separately in a hot pan with a drop of sesame oil, a little of the garlic, and a pinch of salt, about 1 minute per veg. They should stay distinct in colour. Set each aside in its own pile.
Wipe the pan, turn the heat high, and sear the beef in a single layer for 2 minutes until caramelised on the edges.
Heat oil in a non-stick pan and fry the eggs sunny-side up, crispy edges, runny yolk.
Build each bowl: hot rice on the bottom, vegetables arranged in colour-blocked piles around the edge, beef in the centre, fried egg on top.
Spoon over as much gochujang sauce as you like. Scatter nori and sesame. Bring to the table with the sauce on the side for top-ups, and mix vigorously before eating.

notes: The point is contrast, cook each veg separately or they'll all taste the same.
For a proper dolsot bibimbap, use a screaming-hot stone bowl and rub sesame oil around it before adding rice, the crispy bottom layer is the prize.
Soft or runny egg: if you're pregnant, cooking for young children or older people, or have a weakened immune system, cook the egg until the yolk is firm.

title: Biryani
summary: Marinated chicken and parboiled basmati layered with fried onion and saffron, cooked dum.

items.raw: 500g basmati rice, washed and soaked 30 minutes
3 large onions, finely sliced and fried until crisp golden
items.prep: finely sliced and fried until crisp golden

items.raw: Small handful mint and coriander, chopped

items.item: warm milk infused with a pinch of saffron
items.raw: 2 tbsp warm milk infused with a pinch of saffron
250ml neutral oil, for frying the onions

steps.text: Marinate the chicken with all marinade ingredients. Rest at least 1 hour, ideally overnight.
Fry the sliced onions in the oil over medium heat, stirring often, for 15–20 minutes until crisp and golden. Drain on paper towel.
Boil 3 litres of water with the rice spices and salt. When fragrant, add the drained rice. Cook for 5 minutes only, the rice should be 70% done. Drain immediately.
In a heavy pot with a tight lid, melt 2 tbsp ghee. Add the marinated chicken in a single layer. Cook over medium heat for 8 minutes until the yogurt thickens around the meat.
Scatter half the fried onions, mint, and coriander over the chicken.
Spoon the parboiled rice over evenly. Don't mix.
Drizzle the saffron milk, rose water, remaining ghee, and the rest of the fried onions and herbs over the rice.
Seal the lid with foil or a paste of flour and water. Cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes, this is the dum. Don't lift the lid.

Rest 10 minutes off the heat. Check the chicken near the bone reads 75°C; if not, reseal and cook 10 minutes more. Open at the table and scoop straight down through the layers so each plate gets both meat and rice.

notes: Parboiled rice + dum cooking = each grain stays separate. Fully cooked rice up front becomes mush.
Crispy fried onions (birista) are essential. Fry slowly and patiently or buy good ones from an Indian grocer.
Start the day before: the chicken marinates overnight.

title: Black Bean Chili
summary: A meatless chilli of black beans and chipotle, deepened with cocoa and dark chocolate.

items.raw: 2 chipotles in adobo, chopped (+ 1 tbsp adobo sauce)

steps.text: Cook the onion and both capsicums in olive oil for 10 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, chipotles, and all spices including cocoa and cinnamon. Toast 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste; cook 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, stock, and 2 tins of the beans. Simmer 25 minutes, uncovered, stirring occasionally.
Take 2 cups of the chili out, blend, and return, this thickens the base without losing texture.
Add the third tin of beans (kept whole for texture) and the chocolate. Simmer 10 minutes.
Finish with lime juice. Season heavily.
Ladle into bowls. Top with sour cream, cheese, avocado, coriander, spring onion, jalapeños. Crushed chips on top for crunch.

notes: Cocoa and cinnamon. Sounds wrong, tastes deep. The mole influence is the secret.
Half-blend trick gives body without losing whole beans.

title: BLT Sandwich
summary: Crisp bacon, salted ripe tomato and lettuce on thick toast with mustard mayonnaise.

items.raw: 4 thick slices good sourdough (or rustic white bread)

steps.text: Lay the bacon in a cold dry pan. Turn the heat to medium. Cook 8–10 minutes, turning, until deeply crisp. Starting cold renders the fat evenly. Drain on a rack.
Toast the bread to a deep gold, substantial toast holds the sandwich together.
Mix the mayo with mustard and cayenne.
Salt the tomato slices lightly and rest on paper towel for 2 minutes to draw out water (otherwise the bread goes soggy fast).

Build: smear mayo on every cut side of toast. On the bottom slice: lettuce, then tomato (season with salt and pepper), then bacon laid in a tight criss-cross. Top with the second slice mayo-side-down.
Press gently. Cut diagonally with a serrated knife.

notes: Cold pan + bacon = even render. Hot pan = curled, unevenly crisp bacon.
Tomato salted and drained, mayo on every face. Soggy BLT is a sin.

title: Bobotie
summary: Sweetly spiced Cape Malay mince with fruit and almonds, baked under a golden egg custard.

items.raw: 2 tbsp curry powder (Cape Malay style if possible)
2 tbsp Mrs Ball's chutney (or mango chutney)
2 slices white bread, crusts removed, soaked in 120ml milk

steps.text: Heat the oil in a wide pan. Cook the onions 10 minutes until deep golden.
Add the garlic and ginger; cook 1 minute. Add the mince and brown 5 minutes.
Stir in the curry powder, cumin, coriander, turmeric, cinnamon, and cloves. Toast 1 minute.
Add the chutney, jam, vinegar, sultanas, and almonds. Cook 5 minutes.
Squeeze the milk out of the bread (reserve the milk for the custard). Crumble the bread into the mince mixture. Stir well. Season heavily.
Tip the mixture into a baking dish. Press flat. Tuck the bay or lemon leaves into the top.
Whisk the eggs with the reserved milk, the extra milk, turmeric, and salt. Pour over the mince to fully cover.
Bake at 180°C for 35–40 minutes until the custard is set and deeply golden.
Rest 10 minutes. Pluck out the leaves. Serve over yellow rice with chutney and sambal.

notes: Sweet, savoury, slightly fruity, mildly spiced, bobotie is its own category. Don't try to make it taste like Indian curry.
Bay leaves on top is traditional and adds a subtle perfume during baking.

title: Bratwurst
summary: Beer-braised bratwurst seared and piled into rolls with jammy onions and sauerkraut.

steps.text: Melt the butter in a wide pan over medium heat. Add the onions, caraway seeds, and salt. Cook 15 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden.
Push the onions to one side. Add the bratwurst whole. Pour in the beer, it should come halfway up the sausages.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover loosely and cook 12 minutes, turning the sausages once. They're plumping and absorbing flavour.
Lift the sausages out. Crank the heat to reduce the beer-onion liquid until almost all the moisture is gone and the onions are deeply jammy, about 5 minutes.
Return the sausages to the pan. Turn the heat up high and brown them all over for 3 minutes, they should split slightly and develop dark patches, and reach 75°C in the centre.
Split the rolls. Smear with mustard. Pile in beer-braised onions, then a brat, then sauerkraut. Serve with extra mustard.

notes: Beer-braise then sear. Pre-cooking in beer is how to get plump, juicy brats without splitting them open.
Pretzel rolls if you can find them, they make this a proper München lunch.

title: Breakfast Burrito
summary: Crisp potatoes, bacon and soft scrambled eggs rolled in a tortilla and toasted to seal.

steps.text: Cook the diced potato in a wide pan with the olive oil over medium heat for 12 minutes, tossing occasionally, until crisp and golden. Salt heavily. Lift out.
In the same pan, render the bacon for 5 minutes. Add the onion and capsicum; cook 4 minutes. Lift out.
Beat the eggs with milk, salt, and pepper. Melt the butter in the pan over medium-low. Pour in the eggs. Stir gently and constantly until just set but still glossy. Take off the heat immediately.
Warm the tortillas briefly in a dry pan to make pliable.
In the centre of each tortilla, layer: cheese (so it melts against the warm filling), potato, bacon/veg mix, scrambled eggs, more cheese, avocado, salsa, sour cream, hot sauce, coriander.
Fold the bottom over the filling, then fold the sides in tight and roll up.
Toast each burrito seam-side-down in a dry pan for 90 seconds a side, sets the seal and adds a crispy outside.

notes: Cheese against the tortilla on both sides, it melts and acts as glue to keep things contained.
Don't overstuff. A burrito that won't close is just a salad.
Soft scrambled eggs: if you're pregnant, cooking for young children or older people, or have a weakened immune system, cook the eggs until firm.

title: Buffalo Wings
summary: Crackling oven-baked wings tossed in buttery hot sauce with a chunky blue cheese dip.

items.raw: 180ml Frank's RedHot sauce (or similar cayenne-based hot sauce)
Pinch of cayenne for extra heat

steps.text: Pat wings bone dry. Toss with baking powder and salt. Refrigerate uncovered on a rack for at least 1 hour.
Roast at 220°C for 40–45 minutes, flipping once, until deeply golden and crackling.
For the sauce: melt the butter in a small pan over low heat. Whisk in the hot sauce, honey, vinegar, Worcestershire, and garlic. Warm gently, do not boil. Off the heat.
For the blue cheese: mash half the cheese with the sour cream, mayo, buttermilk, and lemon. Stir in the rest of the cheese in chunks. Season with pepper.
Toss the hot wings in the buffalo sauce. Coat every piece.
Pile onto a platter with celery, carrot, and blue cheese for dipping.

notes: Frank's is the original buffalo sauce. Any substitute changes the flavour profile, milder is fine, sweeter (Sriracha) is wrong.
Chunky blue cheese, not smooth. The chunks are part of the dip.

title: Bulgogi
summary: Paper-thin beef marinated with grated pear, seared fast in batches to a sweet glaze.

items.raw: 700g beef rib eye (or sirloin), frozen for 30 minutes then sliced paper-thin against the grain
items.prep: frozen for 30 minutes then sliced paper-thin against the grain

steps.text: Whisk all marinade ingredients in a bowl. Add the sliced beef and massage in. Rest 30 minutes to 2 hours.
Heat a wide heavy pan or wok over high heat until smoking. Add the oil.
Cook the beef in batches, single layer, don't crowd. 90 seconds per batch is enough; the slices cook in seconds. The pear in the marinade caramelises into a glaze.
In the last batch, add the onion, spring onion, and carrot. Toss for 1 minute, keep them crisp.
Combine everything back in the pan, toss 30 seconds to glaze.
Serve over rice with kimchi on the side. Or do ssam: spoon a little rice and beef into a lettuce leaf, dab of ssamjang, fold, eat in one bite.

notes: Slice paper-thin. Partial-freeze the beef first and use your sharpest knife (or ask the butcher).
Grated pear is the Korean tenderiser secret, natural enzymes that do in 30 minutes what marinade can't do in hours.

title: Bunny Chow
summary: Durban lamb and potato curry spooned into a hollowed half-loaf of white bread.

items.raw: 2 tbsp Durban masala (or 1 tbsp curry powder + 1 tbsp Kashmiri chilli powder)
items.note: or 1 tbsp curry powder + 1 tbsp Kashmiri chilli powder

items.item: small loaves of soft white bread
items.raw: 2 small loaves of soft white bread (unsliced), a "quarter" or "half" loaf each

steps.text: Brown the lamb in oil over high heat in batches. Set aside.
In the same pot, cook the onions 12 minutes until deep golden.
Add garlic, ginger, and all whole and ground spices. Toast 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste, then the blitzed tomato. Cook 8 minutes until the oil splits.
Return the lamb. Add the stock and salt. Bring to a simmer. Cover and cook 60 minutes.
Add the potatoes. Cook uncovered 25 minutes more until the lamb is fork-tender and the sauce is thick.
Finish with lemon and coriander.
Cut the loaves in half. Pull out a chunk of the bread interior to make a hollow, keep the chunks for dipping.
Spoon the curry into each bread hollow until overflowing. Sit the bread chunks on top like a hat.
Serve with cucumber and carrot on the side. Eat with your hands, tear bread, scoop curry.

notes: Durban bunny chow originated as workers' lunch, portable curry in bread. The bread bowl is the dish.
Lamb is traditional. Beans (sugar bean curry) is the vegetarian version.

title: Burgers
summary: Smashed beef patties with a deep crust, cheese and a tangy pickle sauce.

items.raw: 800g beef mince (80% lean / 20% fat, chuck is ideal)

steps.text: Mix the sauce ingredients in a bowl. Refrigerate.
Form the mince into 4 loose balls without compressing, handle it as little as possible. Cold mince, light hand.
Heat a heavy pan or cast iron over high heat until smoking. Pour in the oil.
Place each ball in the pan. Press flat with a spatula or burger weight to a 1cm patty. Season the top.
Cook 2.5 minutes, don't move. A deep crust is the goal.
Flip. Lay a slice of cheese on each. Cook 2–3 more minutes, until cooked through with no pink in the middle (75°C). The cheese should drape but not fully melt yet.
In the last minute, butter the buns and toast cut-side down on the hottest part of the pan until deep golden.
Build: bottom bun, sauce, lettuce, tomato, patty (with cheese melt), onion, pickles, sauce on top bun. Press together and let it settle for 30 seconds.

notes: Don't over-handle the mince. Loose balls smashed once in the pan beat formed patties.
A truly hot pan, smoking, gives the Maillard crust that makes a burger taste like a burger.

title: Butter Chicken
summary: Charred thigh pieces in a silky tomato and cream sauce lifted by fenugreek.

items.raw: 700g boneless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces
1 tbsp dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi), crumbled

steps.text: Mix every marinade ingredient in a bowl with the chicken. Cover and rest for at least 30 minutes, ideally a few hours in the fridge.
Heat a heavy pan over high heat until very hot. Add a splash of oil and sear the chicken in batches until the edges char, about 3 minutes per batch. Set aside; it will finish in the sauce.
In the same pan, melt the butter over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 6–8 minutes until soft and golden. Add the ginger and garlic and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes, garam masala, coriander, chilli, sugar, and a splash of water. Simmer 10 minutes until the sauce darkens and thickens.
Blend the sauce smooth with a stick blender for the signature silky texture. Return to the pan.

Stir in the cream and crumbled fenugreek leaves. Slide the chicken (and any juices) back in. Simmer gently for 6–8 minutes until the chicken is cooked through (75°C in the centre) and the sauce coats a spoon.
Taste for salt. Finish with a knob of butter melted in off the heat. Serve with rice or naan, scattered with coriander.

notes: Don't skip the fenugreek leaves, that maple-syrup-meets-curry aroma is what makes it taste like the restaurant version.
Boneless thighs stay juicy; breasts will dry out at this heat.

title: Butternut Squash Risotto
summary: Roasted butternut, half mashed through the rice, finished with sage, walnuts and parmesan.

items.raw: 600g butternut squash, peeled and in 2cm cubes
2 tbsp olive oil, for frying the sage

steps.text: Heat oven to 220°C. Toss squash with oil, cumin, thyme, salt, pepper. Roast 25 minutes until tender and caramelised at edges. Mash half; leave half whole.
While the squash roasts, fry the sage leaves in the olive oil over medium heat for 30 seconds until crisp. Drain on paper towel.
In a wide pan, melt butter with oil. Sweat onion 5 minutes.
Add rice; toast 2 minutes.
Add wine; stir until absorbed.
Add stock a ladle at a time, stirring gently, until the rice is al dente, 16 minutes.
Fold in the mashed squash. Add nutmeg and sage.
Off the heat, mount with cold butter and parmesan.
Plate. Top with the reserved whole squash cubes, walnuts, goat cheese, and crispy sage.

notes: Half mashed, half whole. The mashed melts into the sauce for colour and flavour; the whole gives texture.
Roast the squash first. Boiled squash in risotto = baby food.

title: Caesar Salad
summary: Crisp cos in an anchovy and parmesan dressing with garlic-rubbed sourdough croutons.

items.raw: 3 thick slices sourdough, torn into chunks
4 rashers streaky bacon (optional), cooked crisp and broken

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Toss the bread in olive oil and salt and bake 10–12 minutes, tossing once, until deeply golden. Rub each crouton with the cut side of the garlic clove while still warm.
For the dressing, whisk the yolks, garlic, anchovies, mustard, lemon juice, and Worcestershire in a bowl until smooth.

Whisking constantly, drizzle in the oil in a thin stream until the dressing thickens to thick pouring consistency. Stir in the Parmesan and plenty of pepper. Taste, it should be punchy, salty, lemony.
Tear the larger cos leaves; leave inner ones whole. Drop into a wide bowl.
Spoon over half the dressing and toss to coat every leaf, use clean hands, you'll do a better job than tongs.
Top with croutons, bacon if using, and shavings of Parmesan. Drizzle more dressing. Eat immediately, while everything is crunchy.

notes: Don't skip the anchovies. They don't taste fishy in the dressing, they taste of umami.
Use pasteurised eggs if you're nervous about raw yolks.
The dressing uses raw egg yolks. If you're pregnant, cooking for young children or older people, or have a weakened immune system, use good-quality mayonnaise as the base instead.

title: Calzone
summary: Folded pizza dough filled with ricotta, mozzarella and salami, with sauce for dipping.

items.raw: 1 egg, beaten with 1 tbsp water (for wash)

steps.text: Mix dough ingredients into a shaggy mass. Knead 8 minutes. Cover and rise 90 minutes until doubled.
For the filling: stir together ricotta, mozzarella, parmesan, salami, beaten egg, parsley, salt, pepper, and chilli.
Whisk the sauce ingredients.
Heat the oven to 240°C with a pizza stone inside.
Divide the dough into 4 balls. Roll each into a 22cm circle on a floured bench.
Spoon a quarter of the filling onto one half of each circle, leaving a 2cm border.
Brush the rim with egg wash. Fold the empty half over the filling. Crimp the edges by rolling and pressing with a fork.
Brush the tops with egg wash. Cut 2 small slits in each for steam.
Slide onto the hot stone. Bake 14–16 minutes until deeply golden.
Rest 5 minutes (the filling is molten lava). Serve with the tomato sauce on the side for dipping.

notes: Steam vents are essential, without them, the calzone bursts.
Sauce on the side, not inside. Inside-sauce makes them soggy.

title: Caprese Salad
summary: Ripe heirloom tomatoes, torn buffalo mozzarella and basil with the best olive oil.

items.raw: 4 large ripe heirloom tomatoes (mix colours if you can)
500g good fresh mozzarella di bufala (or fior di latte)
4 tbsp best extra virgin olive oil

steps.text: Bring the mozzarella to room temperature 30 minutes before serving, cold mozzarella tastes of nothing.
Slice the tomatoes into 1cm rounds. Salt them lightly and rest on a board for 3 minutes to release their juices.
Tear the mozzarella into rough pieces (don't slice, tearing exposes more surface for the salt and oil).
On a wide platter, alternate slices of tomato and mozzarella in overlapping rows or pile loosely.
Tuck whole basil leaves between every layer, generous quantities.

Crack pepper over. Drizzle olive oil heavily. Scatter flaky salt at the table. A few drops of aged balsamic if you like, but a great caprese needs nothing but tomato, mozzarella, basil, oil, and salt.

notes: The dish is only as good as the tomatoes. In-season only. Cold-storage tomatoes ruin it.
Mozzarella di bufala if you can find it, the texture is incomparable.

title: Carbonara
summary: Guanciale, egg yolk and pecorino turned into a glossy sauce by the pasta's own heat.

items.raw: 60g pecorino romano, finely grated, plus extra to serve
items.prep: finely grated, plus extra to serve

items.item: Lots of freshly cracked black pepper
items.raw: Lots of freshly cracked black pepper

steps.text: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to the boil. Cook the pasta until just shy of al dente.
Meanwhile, render the guanciale in a cold dry pan over medium heat. Crisp the edges and let the fat melt out, about 6 minutes. Take off the heat.
In a bowl, whisk the yolks, whole egg, and pecorino into a thick paste. Add lots of black pepper.
When the pasta is ready, reserve a mug of pasta water. Drain.
Tip the hot pasta into the pan with the guanciale (off the heat) and toss to coat in the fat.

Now the key move: add a small splash of pasta water to the egg mixture to temper it, then pour over the pasta. Toss vigorously, the residual heat thickens the egg into a glossy cream. If it looks thick, add a splash more water.
Plate immediately. Top with more pecorino and pepper.

notes: Never add cream. The "creaminess" comes from egg yolk + cheese + starchy water.
Pan must be off the heat when the egg hits, or you get scrambled eggs with pasta.
The egg is only lightly cooked by the pasta's heat. If you're pregnant, cooking for young children or older people, or have a weakened immune system, choose a fully cooked pasta dish instead.

title: Carbonnade
summary: A Flemish beef and brown ale stew thickened with mustard-smeared bread.

items.raw: 500ml Belgian brown ale (Chimay, Leffe, or similar)

steps.text: Brown the beef in oil over high heat in batches. Don't crowd. Set aside.
Melt the butter in the same pot. Add the onions and brown sugar. Cook 25 minutes over medium-low heat, stirring often, until deeply caramelised, the colour of dark toffee.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the ale slowly, scraping the base. Add the stock, vinegar, mustard, bay, and thyme.
Return the beef. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Cut the bread to fit on top of the stew. Smear one side heavily with mustard. Float the slices mustard-side-down on the surface, they'll dissolve into the sauce as it cooks, thickening and enriching it.
Cover and bake at 150°C for 2.5 hours until the beef is melting.
Stir the dissolved bread into the sauce. Season, it should taste sweet, malty, slightly tangy.
Serve with fries or potatoes and parsley.

notes: Belgian brown ale gives the malty depth, substitute with a malty British brown ale if needed, never lager.
The mustard bread method is traditional and brilliant. It thickens and seasons at once.

title: Ceviche
summary: Firm white fish cured briefly in lime with chilli and red onion, served with sweet potato.

items.raw: 600g sashimi-grade firm white fish (snapper, sea bass, or barramundi), in 1.5cm cubes
2 ají amarillo chillies, deseeded and finely chopped (or yellow chillies, or 1 mild chilli)
items.note: or yellow chillies, or 1 mild chilli

items.raw: 1 small sweet potato, boiled and cubed

steps.text: Sit the fish cubes in a bowl with the salt for 5 minutes. This firms the flesh and seasons it.
Rinse the red onion in cold water for 5 minutes to soften the bite. Drain.
Pour the lime juice over the fish. The juice should fully cover. Stir gently and rest in the fridge 10 minutes, the fish will turn from translucent to opaque white. This is the "cooking".
Add the chilli, garlic, ginger, celery, and most of the coriander. Stir gently.
Drain off about half the lime juice (called leche de tigre, keep it, it's a Peruvian shot served on the side).
Add the rinsed red onion and toss. Taste and adjust salt and lime.
Plate immediately on chilled bowls with sweet potato, corn, cancha, and avocado around the edge.

notes: Sashimi-grade fish only, the lime denatures protein but doesn't kill pathogens.
Eat within 30 minutes of mixing. Over-marinated ceviche turns chalky.
The fish is cured, not cooked. Not recommended during pregnancy or for anyone with a weakened immune system.

title: Chana Masala
summary: Chickpeas in a tangy tomato and onion gravy sharpened with amchur.

items.raw: 4 ripe tomatoes, blitzed to a puree

steps.text: Heat the ghee in a heavy pot. Add the cumin seeds and let them crackle for 20 seconds.
Add the onions. Cook 10 minutes over medium heat until deeply golden, this colour is the soul of the dish, don't cheat it.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, and green chillies. Cook 1 minute.
Add the tomato puree and paste. Cook 8 minutes, stirring, until the oil splits from the tomato and you see it pooling at the edges.
Tip in the coriander, cumin, turmeric, paprika, and salt. Cook 1 minute to toast.
Add the chickpeas with a splash of water. Simmer 12 minutes, half-covered. Lightly smash a quarter of the chickpeas against the pot to thicken the sauce.
Off the heat, stir in the garam masala and amchur. Rest 5 minutes for the flavours to settle.
Top with coriander and red onion. Serve with rice or bread.

notes: Amchur (dried mango) gives the signature tang. If you can't find it, finish with extra lemon juice.
The deeper the onions caramelise, the better the curry. Take the time.

title: Chicken Adobo
summary: Chicken braised in soy, vinegar, garlic and bay, then reduced to a glossy glaze.

items.raw: 1kg bone-in chicken thighs and drumsticks, skin on

steps.text: In a heavy pot or Dutch oven, combine the chicken with soy, vinegar, garlic, bay, peppercorns, sugar, and water.
Bring to a boil over high heat without stirring. Once it bubbles, reduce to a simmer and cover. Cook 30 minutes.
Uncover and turn the heat to medium-high. Reduce the sauce for 15 minutes, turning the chicken occasionally, until the liquid is glossy and clings to the meat.
Lift the chicken out. Heat the oil in a separate pan over high heat. Crisp the chicken skin-side-down for 3 minutes until deeply browned.
Return to the sauce, toss to coat, and serve over rice with the sauce spooned over.

notes: Don't stir while the vinegar boils off, that's a Filipino kitchen rule and it does change the flavour (less harsh).
The 1:1 soy-to-vinegar ratio is the base. Some families do more soy, some more vinegar. Find your own.

title: Chicken Alfredo
summary: Fettuccine in a butter, cream and parmesan sauce with sliced golden chicken breast.

items.raw: 2 chicken breasts, butterflied to even thickness
120g parmesan, finely grated, plus extra to serve
items.prep: finely grated, plus extra to serve

steps.text: Season the chicken. Heat oil and butter in a wide pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken 4 minutes a side until golden and cooked through (75°C in the thickest part). Rest 5 minutes on a board, then slice.
Cook the pasta in well-salted water until al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water before draining.
While the pasta cooks, melt the butter in a wide pan over low heat. Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds, no colour.
Pour in the cream. Warm through but do not boil. Off the heat, gradually whisk in the parmesan. Add nutmeg and lots of pepper.
Tip the drained pasta straight into the sauce. Toss to coat. Add splashes of pasta water until the sauce clings glossy.
Fold in the sliced chicken. Plate, scatter parsley, finish with more parmesan and pepper.

notes: Authentic Roman alfredo is just butter, parmesan, and pasta water, no cream. This is the American version, which is a different dish that's still delicious.
Off-the-heat cheese whisking stops it clumping. Hot cream + cheese = stringy.

title: Chicken Alfredo Bake
summary: Penne and chicken in a parmesan cream sauce, baked under mozzarella and buttery crumbs.

items.raw: 500g cooked chicken (rotisserie or 2 poached breasts), shredded

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cook the pasta 2 minutes shy of al dente. Drain and toss with the olive oil so it doesn't stick.
In a wide pan, melt the butter. Cook the garlic 30 seconds. Add the cream and warm through.
Off the heat, whisk in the parmesan, Italian seasoning, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Sauce should be silky.
Toss the pasta and shredded chicken through the sauce.
Tip into a baking dish. Top with mozzarella, parmesan, and the buttery panko.
Bake 22 minutes until bubbling and the top is deep golden.
Rest 5 minutes. Scatter parsley. Serve.

notes: The sauce is the same as chicken alfredo but baked dish gets a crunchy top, best of both.
Undercook the pasta. It absorbs in the oven and goes mushy if started al dente.

title: Chicken and Rice
summary: Crisp-skinned thighs baked over turmeric and lemon rice that soaks up the pan juices.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C. Season chicken with paprika, salt, pepper.
Heat oil in a wide oven-safe pan over medium-high. Brown chicken skin-side-down 6 minutes, flip 3 more minutes. Lift out.
Drain all but 2 tbsp fat. Cook onion 5 minutes. Add garlic; 30 seconds.
Add rice. Toast 90 seconds. Add turmeric.
Pour in stock. Add bay leaf, lemon zest. Bring to simmer.
Nestle chicken on top, skin-side-up. Cover and bake at 180°C for 30 minutes.
Lift the lid for the last 5 minutes to re-crisp the skin.
Check the thickest thigh reaches 75°C, then rest 10 minutes covered. Fluff rice. Scatter parsley. Serve with lemon and sauce.

notes: One-pan magic. The rice absorbs all the chicken fat and stock.
Lemon zest infuses through the rice as it steams. Adds brightness.

title: Chicken and Waffles
summary: Buttermilk fried chicken on light waffles with warm maple syrup and hot honey.

steps.text: Marinate the chicken with buttermilk, hot sauce, the 1 tbsp salt and pepper. Rest at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Mix flour, cornflour, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, cayenne, and the 1 tsp salt for the coating.
Lift each piece of chicken out of the buttermilk (let excess drip off) and press into the seasoned flour, getting deep into the crevices for craggy texture. Lay on a rack and rest 15 minutes.

Heat oil in a deep heavy pan to 165°C. Fry the chicken in batches for 12–15 minutes per batch (thighs), turning, until deep golden and internal temperature hits 75°C. Drain on a rack and keep warm in a low oven.
For waffles: whisk the dry ingredients. Whisk the egg yolks, buttermilk, butter, and vanilla. Combine wet and dry just until smooth. Whip the egg whites to soft peaks; fold in gently.
Heat a waffle iron. Pour in batter and cook per machine until deep golden.
Plate: waffle, fried chicken on top, drizzle maple syrup, dot hot honey if you like, butter on the waffle. Eat with hands.

notes: Buttermilk marinade overnight is the entire secret to juicy fried chicken.
Sweet syrup + salty chicken + heat = the holy trinity.
Start in the morning or the day before: the chicken marinates for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.

title: Chicken Biryani
summary: Marinated chicken under parboiled spiced basmati, sealed and cooked dum with saffron.

items.raw: Small handful chopped mint and coriander
500g basmati rice, washed and soaked 30 minutes
3 large onions, finely sliced and fried until crisp golden (birista)
items.prep: finely sliced and fried until crisp golden

items.item: warm milk infused with a pinch of saffron
items.raw: 2 tbsp warm milk infused with a pinch of saffron
125ml neutral oil, for frying the onions

steps.text: Marinate the chicken at least 1 hour, ideally overnight.
Fry the onions: heat the oil in a wide pan over medium heat and fry the sliced onions, stirring often, for 15–20 minutes until crisp and deep golden. Drain on paper towel.
Boil 3 litres of water with the rice spices and salt. Add the drained rice. Cook 5 minutes only, 70% done. Drain.
In a heavy pot, melt 2 tbsp ghee. Lay the marinated chicken in a single layer. Cook 15 minutes, turning once, until the yogurt thickens around the chicken and it's nearly cooked through.
Scatter half the fried onions, mint, and coriander over the chicken.
Spoon the parboiled rice over evenly. Don't mix.
Drizzle saffron milk, rose water, remaining ghee, and rest of fried onions and herbs over the rice.
Seal the lid with foil or a paste of flour and water. Cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes, this is the dum. The chicken should reach 75°C at the bone.
Rest 10 minutes off the heat. Open at the table and scoop straight down through the layers.

notes: Same dum-cooking method as plain biryani, what makes this distinct is the marinated chicken under the rice.
Crispy fried onions are the soul. Fry them properly or buy good ones from an Indian grocer.
Start at least an hour ahead: the chicken marinates for 1 hour, ideally overnight.

title: Chicken Burrito Bowl
summary: Charred spiced chicken over lime rice with beans, corn, pico de gallo and avocado.

steps.text: Marinate the chicken in spices, oil, lime, garlic, salt. Rest 15 minutes.
Heat a heavy pan over high heat. Cook chicken in a single layer 4 minutes a side until charred and cooked through.
Toss the rice with coriander, lime, oil, salt.
Build each bowl: rice on one side, beans alongside, then chicken on top. Add corn, pico, avocado, cheese, sour cream, jalapeños. Lime wedge.

notes: Make ahead, eat all week. The rice and beans hold; chicken reheats well.
Lime + coriander rice is what makes it taste like Chipotle.
Cool any cooked rice quickly (spread it out on a tray), refrigerate it within an hour and reheat it until steaming hot.

title: Chicken Caesar Pasta
summary: Pasta in an anchovy, parmesan and cream sauce with chicken, bacon, croutons and cos.

items.raw: 4 rashers streaky bacon, fried crisp and broken

steps.text: Cook chicken: season, sear 4 minutes a side in oil until cooked through (75°C in the thickest part). Rest, then slice.
Cook pasta until just shy of al dente. Reserve a mug of pasta water; drain.
In a wide pan, melt butter. Add garlic and anchovies; sizzle 90 seconds, anchovies dissolve.
Add cream, mustard, Worcestershire. Warm but don't boil.
Off the heat, whisk in parmesan and lemon. Plenty of pepper.
Tip pasta into sauce. Toss with a splash of pasta water.
Fold in sliced chicken and most of the bacon.
Plate. Top with crushed croutons, shredded lettuce, shaved parmesan, remaining bacon, chives.

notes: The lettuce on TOP is the move. Wilted lettuce in hot pasta is wrong.
Anchovies. Don't skip. They make the sauce, not fish.

title: Chicken Caesar Wrap
summary: Sliced chicken, bacon, cos and crushed croutons rolled with a punchy Caesar dressing.

items.raw: 4 rashers streaky bacon, fried crisp and broken

steps.text: Season the chicken with oil, oregano, salt, and pepper. Cook in a hot pan 4 minutes a side until golden and cooked through (75°C in the thickest part). Rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Whisk the dressing ingredients. Taste, should be sharp and umami.
Warm each tortilla briefly in a dry pan to make pliable.
In the centre of each tortilla, spread a stripe of dressing.
Pile on shredded lettuce, sliced chicken, bacon, croutons, and shaved parmesan. Drizzle more dressing on top.
Fold the bottom up over the filling, then fold the sides in tight and roll up.
Optional: toast the wraps seam-side-down in a dry pan for 1 minute a side to set them.

notes: Caesar without anchovy isn't Caesar. They don't taste fishy, they taste of umami.
Crushed croutons work better than whole in a wrap; whole croutons poke holes.

title: Chicken Cordon Bleu
summary: Chicken rolled around ham and Gruyère, double-crumbed and baked, with a Dijon cream sauce.

steps.text: Pound the chicken breasts to even 5mm thickness between cling film.
On each breast, lay a slice of ham, then a slice of cheese. Roll up tightly, tucking the ends in. Secure with 2 toothpicks each, or chill 30 minutes for a tighter roll.
Set up flour, egg, and panko mixed with parmesan and thyme.
Dredge each roll in flour, then egg, then panko. Press firmly. Then back through egg and panko again for a double-crumb seal, this stops the cheese leaking.
Heat the oil and butter in a wide oven-safe pan over medium-high. Brown each roll for 90 seconds on all 4 sides, about 6 minutes total.
Transfer the pan to a 200°C oven. Bake 12 minutes until the chicken is cooked through (75°C internal).
For the sauce: melt butter in a separate pan, cook shallot 3 minutes. Pour in wine; reduce by half. Add cream and mustard. Simmer 3 minutes. Season with nutmeg, salt, pepper.
Remove toothpicks. Slice each roll on the diagonal. Plate with sauce spooned around (not over, the panko must stay crisp). Sprinkle parsley.

notes: Double-crumb the rolls. Single coats blow out when the cheese melts.
Sauce around, not over. Keep the crust crisp.

title: Chicken Enchilada Casserole
summary: Layers of tortilla, chicken, beans and corn baked in red chilli sauce with melted cheese.

items.raw: 500ml enchilada sauce (or homemade red chilli sauce)

steps.text: Heat oven to 200°C.
Cook onion in olive oil 5 minutes. Add garlic and spices; cook 1 minute. Take off heat. Stir in shredded chicken, beans, and corn. Season.
Pour a thin layer of enchilada sauce into a deep baking dish.
Cover with a layer of torn corn tortillas. Top with half the chicken mixture, a third of the remaining sauce, a third of the cheese.
Repeat: tortillas, chicken, sauce, cheese. Top with final layer of tortillas, remaining sauce, and the last third of cheese.
Cover with foil. Bake 20 minutes. Uncover and bake another 12 minutes until bubbling and the cheese is deep golden.
Rest 5 minutes. Top with sour cream, avocado, jalapeños, coriander, spring onion, feta. Lime wedges on the side.

notes: Stacked casserole skips the rolling step. Same flavour, less work.
Cold toppings on hot casserole. The contrast is the dish.

title: Chicken Fajita Bowl
summary: Charred chicken and capsicum over lime rice with beans, pico de gallo and avocado.

items.raw: 2 cups cooked cilantro lime rice (rice tossed with lime, coriander, oil)
items.note: rice tossed with lime, coriander, oil

steps.text: Mix the chicken with the marinade. Rest 15 minutes.
Heat a cast iron pan over screaming-high heat. Cook the chicken in batches in a single layer for 3 minutes a side until charred and cooked through. Lift out.
In the same pan, sear the capsicum and onion with oil and salt, char on the edges, crunch in the middle, about 4 minutes total.
Build each bowl: rice on one side, beans alongside, chicken and veg over the top. Pile on pico, avocado, cheese, sour cream, jalapeño.
Squeeze of lime and dash of hot sauce.

notes: Hot pan, single layer. Crowded pan steams instead of chars.
Pre-cook all components, then assemble. Reheat-friendly for meal prep.
Cool any cooked rice quickly (spread it out on a tray), refrigerate it within an hour and reheat it until steaming hot.

title: Chicken Fried Rice
summary: Cold rice fried hard in a smoking wok with chicken, egg, peas and soy.

items.raw: 4 cups cold cooked jasmine rice (day-old is ideal)

steps.text: Break up the cold rice with your fingers so every grain is separate. This is the whole technique.
Mix the sauce ingredients in a small bowl.
Heat a wok over high heat until smoking. Add 1 tbsp oil. Cook the chicken 3 minutes until cooked through. Lift out.
Add another tbsp oil. Pour in the eggs. Let them set for 5 seconds, then scramble into rough curds. Lift out.
Add the last tbsp oil. Stir-fry the onion and carrot for 2 minutes. Add the garlic and ginger; toss 30 seconds.
Add the cold rice. Spread it across the wok and let it sit for 30 seconds to crisp the bottom. Then break it up and toss continuously for 2 minutes, those crispy bits are gold.
Return the chicken and egg. Add the peas. Toss to combine.
Pour the sauce around the edges of the wok. Toss for 60 seconds until every grain is glossy and brown.
Off the heat, fold in spring onions. Plate immediately.

notes: Cold rice or no rice. Fresh hot rice turns to mush in the wok.
Wok screaming hot. The Cantonese call this wok hei, breath of the wok. It tastes of high heat.
If you cook rice for this, spread it on a tray to cool quickly, then refrigerate within an hour. Don't leave cooked rice sitting out.

title: Chicken Fried Steak
summary: Double-dredged cube steak fried crisp and smothered in a peppery cream gravy.

items.raw: 4 beef cube steaks (or pounded thin minute steaks), about 200g each
3 tbsp of the frying oil from above (with brown bits)

steps.text: Pound the steaks thin if not already. Season heavily.
Combine the flour with garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Whisk the eggs with buttermilk and hot sauce.
Dredge each steak in seasoned flour, dip in egg-buttermilk, then back into the flour. Double-coat for crunch.
Heat 1cm of oil in a wide cast iron pan to 175°C.
Fry the steaks 3 minutes a side until deep golden. Drain on a rack.
For the gravy: pour out all but 3 tbsp of the oil, keeping the brown bits in the pan. Reduce heat to medium.
Whisk in the flour. Cook 2 minutes until pale brown.
Whisk in the milk gradually. Simmer 4 minutes until thick. Salt heavily. Crack a stupid amount of black pepper in, it makes the gravy.
Plate the steak over mash. Ladle gravy generously. Sides on the plate.

notes: Double-dredge for the proper craggy crust.
White pepper gravy is the Southern way. Don't hold back on the black pepper.

title: Chicken Gyoza
summary: Pleated chicken and cabbage dumplings fried, steamed and re-crisped on the base.

items.raw: 200g finely shredded napa cabbage, salted with 1 tsp and squeezed dry
items.prep: salted with 1 tsp and squeezed dry

steps.text: Mix the filling: combine everything in a bowl and stir vigorously in one direction for 2 minutes, this is what gives gyoza their springy texture.
Set up a small bowl of water. Place a wrapper in your palm. Spoon a heaped teaspoon of filling in the centre.
Wet half the wrapper edge with a finger. Fold in half, then make 5–6 pleats on the front side, pressing each pleat firmly against the flat back. The dumpling sits up flat-bottomed.
Repeat. Lay completed gyoza on a tray dusted with cornflour so they don't stick.

Working in two batches, heat 1.5 tbsp oil in a wide non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Arrange the gyoza flat-side-down in a circular pattern, snug together. Cook 2 minutes until the bases are deep golden.
Pour in half the water (it will sputter). Cover immediately with a lid. Steam 5 minutes, until the filling is cooked through (75°C).
Uncover. Let the remaining water evaporate, 2 more minutes. The bases will re-crisp.
Slide the whole pan onto a plate upside-down so the crispy bases face up.
Whisk the dipping sauce. Serve immediately.

notes: Mix the filling in one direction, that's the Japanese trick for bouncy texture.
Fry-then-steam-then-fry-again gives the signature crispy bottom and soft top.

title: Chicken Gyro
summary: Charred oregano and lemon chicken in warm pita with tzatziki, tomato and hot chips.

steps.text: Marinate the chicken with all listed ingredients. Rest at least 1 hour.
Whisk the tzatziki. Refrigerate.
Heat a heavy pan or grill plate to screaming-high. Cook the chicken in batches in a single layer, 3 minutes a side until charred at the edges and cooked through.
Warm the pita briefly over an open flame or in a dry pan.
Build: pita, tzatziki, lettuce or salad if you like, chicken, tomato, onion, a few hot chips inside, more tzatziki, lemon squeeze. Roll tight.

notes: Chicken thighs over breast, they take the char.
Chips inside the wrap. It's Greek; that's how it's done.

title: Chicken Gyudon
summary: Chicken and onion simmered in sweet dashi and soy, spooned over rice with an egg.

steps.text: In a wide pan, combine dashi, soy, mirin, sake, sugar, ginger. Simmer.
Add onions. Cook 5 minutes until softening.
Slide the chicken in. Cook 5 minutes until cooked through and the sauce reduces enough to cling to the meat.
Mound rice in deep bowls. Ladle chicken and onions on top with plenty of sauce that soaks into the rice.
Crack the raw egg over the hot meat (it tempers and creates a sauce) or top with a soft-boiled egg, halved.
Scatter pickled ginger, spring onion, shichimi.

notes: Same technique as beef gyudon, just swap protein.
Soft yolk + savoury sauce + sweet onions over rice. Japanese comfort food.
Raw or soft-cooked egg isn't recommended if you're pregnant, cooking for young children or older people, or have a weakened immune system. Use a hard-boiled egg instead.

title: Chicken Katsu
summary: Panko-crumbed chicken fried crisp, served with rice, shredded cabbage and tonkatsu sauce.

items.raw: 4 chicken breasts, butterflied and pounded to 1.5cm

steps.text: Whisk the tonkatsu sauce ingredients in a bowl. Done.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Set up three shallow dishes: flour, egg, panko. Dredge each cutlet in flour (shake off excess), dip in egg, then press firmly into panko, coating both sides. Press hard, every crumb should stick.
Heat 1cm of oil in a wide pan to 170°C (a panko crumb should sizzle vigorously).
Fry the cutlets 3 minutes a side until deep golden, crisp and 75°C in the thickest part. Drain on a rack, paper towel makes the bottom soggy.
Rest 2 minutes, then slice across the grain into 2cm strips.
Plate over rice with a heap of cabbage, mayo on the cabbage, sesame on top, and lemon on the side. Tonkatsu sauce in a small bowl for dipping.

notes: Panko, not regular breadcrumbs, that's the whole texture.
A rack, not paper. Anything that traps steam ruins the crunch.

title: Chicken Kiev
summary: Double-crumbed chicken breast sealed around frozen garlic butter that floods out when cut.

steps.text: Beat together the butter, garlic, parsley, lemon zest, salt, and pepper. Shape into a log on cling film and freeze for 30 minutes until firm.
Cut a deep horizontal pocket into the thickest side of each chicken breast, almost all the way through.
Cut the frozen butter log into 4 equal pieces. Stuff one piece deep into each pocket and press the chicken closed.
